sections.text: Arjuna asked: My Lord! Who is God and what is Nature; what is Matter and what is the Self; what is that they call Wisdom, and what is it that is worth knowing? I wish to have this explained.
Lord Shri Krishna replied: O Arjuna! The body of man is the playground of the Self; and That which knows the activities of Matter, sages call the Self.
क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत।
I am the Omniscient self that abides in the playground of Matter; knowledge of Matter and of the all-knowing Self is wisdom.

We concluded chapter 12, bhakti yoga, Yoga of Devotion. Now well be starting discussion on Chapter 13, the Kshetra Kshetrajna Vibhaga Yoga, Yoga of differentiation between the field and its knower. So far we have seen the two segments of the Bhagavad Gita which discussed tat and tvam from the Mahavakya Tattvamasi.
The first six chapters we learned about tvam. The next six chapters we learned about tat. Now we will be discussing the correlative verb asi, the connections between the two and how to differentiate between the two. Therefore its called Kshetra Kshetrajna Vibhaga Yoga, Yoga of the field and its knower. In other words, how to differentiate between what I am not and what I am.
There is a granth written by Bhagavan Shankaracharya, or at least attributed to him, called Drig Drishya Viveka, which is similar in nature but more logically explained. Drig Drishya Viveka -- discrimination between the seer and the seen. Who is the seer and what is seen? If we can differentiate, then we know them both.
So the same way, here it says Kshetra Kshetrajna Vibhaga -- how to differentiate the field from its knower. So thats the theme of this chapter. In other words, we will be learning how to navigate through maya.
Maya is the entity which creates this confusion for me, who I am and what is my real nature. Maya creates this illusion of plurality where the only singularity exists. One exists, but it appears to be many.
So the chapter now discusses this aspect of Maya in detail. In this chapter, suddenly after devotion, Krishna took up a theme which is completely different, and therefore some interpolator has added this one verse. The very first verse, Arjuna Uvacha, does not appear in previous commentators commentaries.
Bhagavan Shankaracharya did not comment on the first verse; he starts from the second verse. Same with Jnaneshwari -- it also starts from the second verse. Because it seemed like Bhagavan had suddenly taken up a different topic, somebody thought it appropriate to add a connector between what was discussed so far and what would be discussed next.
What we will be discussing is actually the continuation of the theme. Bhagavan started this theme in chapter seven and chapter eight. In chapter seven he talked about the Eightfold Lower Prakriti and the Manifest Prakriti.
Then in chapter eight he talked about the imperishable Brahman. Chapters nine, ten, and eleven were somewhat of a distraction from the theme because Arjuna kept asking questions. He wanted to know in what different forms to think about Bhagavan, so Krishna gave the Vibhuti yoga.
Then he wanted to know Bhagavan in his totality, so Krishna gave him the Vishwarupadarshan. And then obviously it culminated in Bhakti Yoga. So Bhagavan picked up that theme again from chapters 7 and 8.
In chapter 13, we want to continue the theme of how to differentiate between the Jiva and Paramatma and what is their connection. As we have learnt in that great statement: that which you are seeking, and you who consider who you are, are one and the same. But right now I dont see the connection.
Once I know the nature of both, then I will be able to connect them. So thats basically the theme of chapter 13, Kshetra Kshetrajna Vibhaga Yoga. The very first verse, Arjuna Uvacha, basically gives you what were going to discuss in this chapter.
As weve discussed many times, the best presentation is when you first tell them what youre going to talk about, then tell them what you are talking about, and then tell them what you told them. Summarize it, put an agenda up front, make the presentation, and then summarize. So here the first verse attributed to Arjuna says: Prakritim Purusham cha eva, Kshetram Kshetrajnam eva cha, etat veditum icchami, Jnanam Jneyam cha Keshava.
These are the things I want to understand clearly. We pick up the themes from chapters 7 and 8. Prakritim Purusham -- I want to know Prakriti and Purusha.
We have discussed these before; we need to brush up our knowledge of what Prakriti and Purusha are. And also Kshetra Kshetrajna, the field and its Knower. You talked about the field of my actions.
This world currently is clear to me -- this is the field of my actions. For me it is very simple. I am the actor and this world is the field of my actions.
So I am the knower of the field of my actions. But when it comes to knowing who I am, I have to go further. So we will talk about that.
Kshetram Kshetrajnam eva cha, etat veditum icchami, Jnanam Jneyam cha Keshava -- I also want to know what is knowledge and what is to be known. So we clarified by this first verse what well be discussing. To know myself, I have to be very clear about what is Prakriti and what is Purusha, what is manifest and what is unmanifest.
I also need to know what is the field of my activity and who is the actor. I also want to know what is knowledge and what is to be known. Just simple curiosity -- I want to know -- doesnt mean anything.
I need to know what is there to be known. So Arjuna asked this question to put the agenda forward for this chapter, saying we want to know about these things. The next verse is where it changes the paradigm for us.
Idam shariram Kaunteya, Kshetram iti abhidhiyate -- this body, O Kaunteya, is called the field. Completely different than what I thought all along. We thought that this world is the field, and I as this limited being am the knower of this world.
I know my world, I know my field -- my field of profession, field of activity. So right now I have considered this body to be the knower, this me, this limited being, to be me. But Bhagavan said no, this body itself is the field.
This field which I consider to be the world, and this body, mind, intellect which I consider to be me -- He said no, this body belongs to the field, the Prakriti. The knower is somebody different than that. This body is called the field.
He who knows is called the Kshetrajna. One who knows this body is the Kshetrajna. Once I have established what the field is, the one who knows the field is the knower.
So from the perspective of the world, the I is the seer of this world. When I see colors and forms, my eye is the seer and the world is the seen. When it comes to my eye, the mind is the seer and the eye is the seen.
When I observe what is happening to my eye, who is seeing? My mind is seeing my eye. So I took a step backward and put the seer in the field of the seen. And if I keep receding, then everything that I consider today to be me will belong to the field of Prakriti.
That which I consider to be me so far is my mind, my body, my intellect. Thats what I define myself to be. But when seen from the perspective of what do I know, I know about my body.
If I know my body, then I am the the knower. Somebody other than my body. Same goes for my mind.
Im very aware that my mind is upset. So I am the knower of my mind. My mind is not calm today.
Somebody sees the mind to be not calm or calm -- there is some other entity which is seeing the mind. That same entity also can judge whether my intellect is sharp or dull. I dont know about it.
So there is somebody other than this body, mind and intellect who is the knower. One who knows all these three. So in short, Bhagavan says the body is the field.
The one who knows that is considered to be the knower. Thats basically simple. But because of my identification, I always considered this to be the seer.
As I give the example that my eye can see but only with the aid of my glasses. So I consider the glasses to be as important as my eye. If I want to read without glasses, I cannot read.
So glasses are as important for me to read as my eye is. But I dont consider my eye and glasses in the same category. Because I know I can go to LensCrafters and get replacement glasses in one hour.
The eye, at least today, is not that easy to replace. Someday it will probably be as simple. Till that time, I consider the eye to be something very special -- part of me without which I cannot see.
But glasses I can replace. But if I can now learn that even the eye can be replaced anytime, then I will also put the eye in the same category as my glasses. Sometimes the instruments through which we see, we identify with so closely that we forget the differentiation between the seer and the seen.
So Bhagavan changes this paradigm and says this body is the field through which the seer is functioning to manifest. Electricity needs all these lamps and gadgets. Electricity is present in this room -- we can vouch for it because the lights are on, the air conditioning is on.
But remove both the air conditioning and the light, and we will not know whether electricity is in the room or not -- until you put a finger in that outlet. So the seer is present, but its presence is felt through the equipment. The knower is only there as long as the knowables are there.
If theres nothing to be known, the knower is not needed. The proverbial question -- whether a tree falling in the jungle makes a sound or not -- unless theres somebody to listen to that sound, the world of sound does not exist. And unless there are objects, no knower can exist.
In my deep sleep, there is no knower because the world does not exist for me. Therefore there is no knower. If there are no knowables, the knower does not exist.
So if you remove the knowables from the knower, Bhagavan says, what remains is pure knowledge -- not knowledge of something, but knowledge by itself, which we call pure awareness. Right now I exist as something. Then everything else follows -- as Rajan, as an architect, as a father, as a community member, whatever it is.
But I have to attach something to I exist. And if you remove all of them, what remains is simply I exist. So the knower and the known go together. So it says, idam shariram Kaunteya, Kshetram iti abhidhiyate. This body is to be known as the field, and the one who knows the body is the knower of the field.
Now these are the arguments for us to navigate through Maya so that you can contemplate on the nature of the self. You can start to contemplate: okay, if this body is not me, who knows this body? The next verse says, Kshetrajnam cha api mam viddhi, sarva-kshetreshu Bharata. Once we have discussed that this body is the field and the knower is the Kshetrajna, then we may have another confusion -- that in my body I am the field and my consciousness is the knower.
In your body, the same thing for you. There are so many knowers in this world, as many beings are there that many knowers are there from our perspective from just learning the second verse. So Bhagavan clarifies this.

These opening verses introduce the revolutionary insight that idam shariram - this very body - is the field (kshetra), not just the external world. Krishna declares that there is only one Knower (kshetrajna) in all fields. Today, contemplate this paradigm shift: you have always considered your body, mind, and intellect to be you - the knower. But what if they belong to the field of the known? Spend a few moments simply observing your body sensations, your thoughts, your emotional reactions. Notice that there is something aware of all these - that awareness itself is the true Knower.
The verse states kshetra-kshetrajnayor jnanam yat taj jnanam matam mama - the knowledge of both field and Knower is true wisdom. This week, practice asking yourself throughout the day: Who is aware of this experience right now? When you notice your breath, who notices? When you feel an emotion, who feels aware of that feeling? This inquiry is the beginning of navigating through Maya - the confusion between what you are not and what you truly are.
As a practical exercise, sit quietly for five minutes each morning. Let your attention rest on the simple sense of I exist before any thought of being a particular person with particular roles. Can you touch that pure sense of existence-awareness before the mind adds labels? This is the doorway to understanding the Knower of the field.
